rules.title: Explicit boundary ownership
rules.description: Every changed cross-layer or cross-module boundary has one canonical owner and an explicit direction.

rules.title: Canonical ownership
rules.description: A concept, state transition, or business invariant has exactly one authoritative owner.

rules.title: No inverted or internal dependency
rules.description: Code must not reverse the registered dependency direction or import another module's internal implementation.

rules.title: Concrete-first abstraction
rules.description: Introduce abstractions only after a concrete boundary or repeated variation demonstrates the need.

rules.title: Minimal architectural change
rules.description: Use the smallest architectural change that satisfies the accepted task contract.

rules.title: Explicit boundary contracts
rules.description: Public, cross-module, persisted, external, and asynchronous boundaries use an explicit versioned contract.

rules.title: Domain and API representation separation
rules.description: Domain objects are not used as transport, persistence, or generated client representations without an explicit mapping boundary.

rules.title: Canonical source of truth
rules.description: Generated and derived artifacts identify their canonical input and are reproducible from it.

rules.title: Business-oriented naming
rules.description: Structure and names express business capabilities rather than accidental framework layers.

rules.title: Boundary-oriented tests
rules.description: Changed boundaries have conformance or regression coverage at the boundary where failure is observable.

rules.title: Minimal legacy refactoring
rules.description: Unrelated legacy behavior is preserved and refactoring is limited to what the task requires.

rules.title: Project identity decides layout
rules.description: domain/api-contract/backend/frontend are references only; project identity and registered contexts decide the real layout.
